checks.name: Check that field child_given_names has invalid_count = 0
checks.qualityDefinition:
customProperties:
- property: check_id
  value: data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.child_given_names.invalidValues_datacontract
- property: introduced_date
  value: '2026-09-15'
- property: changelog
  value: '[]'
description: |
  A name should be letters, spaces, periods, and hyphens only - a digit or a symbol like "/" means a form was submitted incomplete (e.g. "N/A") or a test/dummy record leaked into the real feed (e.g. "Baby1"). Honest limitation: this is a character-set check, not a dictionary of known junk words - DuckDB's regex engine (RE2, the same engine Soda's checks compile down to) has no lookahead support, so a purely alphabetic junk word like a bare "TEST" or "UNKNOWN" with no digit or symbol in it would NOT be caught by this rule alone.
dimension: conformity
severity: error
metric: invalidValues
arguments:
  pattern: ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z. -]*$
mustBe: 0
checks.implementation:
SELECT
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN NOT (
        "t0"."child_given_names" IS NULL
      )
      AND NOT (
        REGEXP_MATCHES("t0"."child_given_names", '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z. -]*$')
      )
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS "birth_registrations__child_given_names__field_invalid_values"
FROM "birth_registrations" AS "t0"

description: |
  Guards against a type/format change upstream (e.g. a datetime-with-timezone field arriving where a plain date is expected) turning into silently unparseable or nonsensical dates downstream.
dimension: conformity
severity: error
type: sql
mustBe: 0
query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {model} WHERE {field} < DATE '1900-01-01' OR {field} >
  CURRENT_DATE
checks.implementation: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM birth_registrations WHERE date_of_birth < DATE '1900-01-01' OR date_of_birth > CURRENT_DATE

checks.name: Freshness / relative-date check: if no record in this batch has a date_of_birth within 7 days of THIS RUN's own date_registered, the upstream feed has likely gone stale - still delivering files, but with old or replayed data. Phase 5f (plans/qa-pipeline.md #61, 2026-09-17): previously compared against real wall-clock CURRENT_DATE instead, which made this check permanently red as real time drifted from this fixture's fixed dates - anchoring to date_registered fixes that (every row's date_registered is exactly this run's own run_date by construction - see daily_batch.py's own comment), same fix as the dbt/Soda versions of this check. Anchoring alone isn't enough on its own, though: ordinary registration lag (0-9 days on every row, independent of any defect) already puts most rows within the 7-day window, so this would trivially always pass without generator/dirty.py's new inject_stale_delivery - an occasional whole-run defect that pushes every row's date_of_birth 15-45 days before date_registered, giving this check something genuine to occasionally catch.
checks.qualityDefinition:
customProperties:
- property: check_id
  value: data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.date_of_birth.freshness_datacontract
- property: introduced_date
  value: '2026-01-15'
- property: changelog
  value: '[{"date": "2026-09-17T00:00:00Z", "description": "Anchored to this run''s
    own date_registered instead of real wall-clock CURRENT_DATE, which is why this
    check was permanently red. Paired with a new inject_stale_delivery generator defect
    so the check has something genuine to catch.", "author": "Keith Moss", "breaking":
    true}]'
description: |
  Freshness / relative-date check: if no record in this batch has a date_of_birth within 7 days of THIS RUN's own date_registered, the upstream feed has likely gone stale - still delivering files, but with old or replayed data. Phase 5f (plans/qa-pipeline.md #61, 2026-09-17): previously compared against real wall-clock CURRENT_DATE instead, which made this check permanently red as real time drifted from this fixture's fixed dates - anchoring to date_registered fixes that (every row's date_registered is exactly this run's own run_date by construction - see daily_batch.py's own comment), same fix as the dbt/Soda versions of this check. Anchoring alone isn't enough on its own, though: ordinary registration lag (0-9 days on every row, independent of any defect) already puts most rows within the 7-day window, so this would trivially always pass without generator/dirty.py's new inject_stale_delivery - an occasional whole-run defect that pushes every row's date_of_birth 15-45 days before date_registered, giving this check something genuine to occasionally catch.
dimension: timeliness
severity: error
type: sql
mustBe: 0
query: |
  SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM {model} WHERE {field} >= date_registered - INTERVAL 7 DAY
checks.implementation: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM birth_registrations WHERE date_of_birth >= date_registered - INTERVAL 7 DAY
